# Decorators and type wrappers

Every decorator the core registers, grouped by the authoring package a
schema file imports it from, and the type wrappers beside them. An
extension's decorators come from its own package.

Each entry gives the TypeScript declaration `tsc` checks a schema file
against, its comment, the nodes it may sit on (a type is a class with
fields, an operation set a class with methods, an operation a method)
and the kinds it is limited to when it is. The JSON and YAML forms write
a decorator's argument as a JSON value; `superschematic json-schema`
prints the schema the loader checks it against, for every decorator the
binary you run knows, an extension's too.

## Which kinds may import a package

Operation sets and operations exist only in API schemas. Every kind may
import `superscalar` and the packages not listed here.

| Package | Kinds that may import it |
| --- | --- |
| `@superschematic/schema` | API, Bucket, DB, General, Site, Stack |
| `@superschematic/db` | DB |
| `@superschematic/api` | API |
| `@superschematic/schema-config` | API, Bucket, DB, General, Site, Stack |
| `@superschematic/stack` | Stack |

## `@superschematic/schema`

### `@behavior`

```ts
function behavior<N extends BehaviorName>(
  name: N,
  ..._config: BehaviorConfigArg<N>
): ClassDecorator
```

Composes a behavior on a type: code that adds fields, operations, checks
and storage to the type when an engine runs the schema. Several apply in
source order, and a type lists a behavior once. The config is a literal,
checked against the behavior's declaration when the schema loads.

- On a type declaration.
- Each behavior, its config and what it adds to a type: [behaviors.md](behaviors.md).

### `@denyUnknownFields`

```ts
const denyUnknownFields: ClassDecorator
```

Make the generated Rust serde deserializer reject a payload key the type
does not declare instead of dropping it (#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]).
Opt-in per type: strict decoding suits a closed wire contract, where a
misspelled key silently disappearing is the failure, and breaks a payload
that has to survive a producer newer than its consumer.

- On a type declaration.

### `@display`

```ts
function display(config: DisplayConfig): ClassDecorator
function display(config: FieldDisplayConfig): PropertyDecorator
```

Says how a UI, or an agent, renders the type's instances. It adds no
field, operation or storage, and changes no generated code. The loader
holds the fields it names to the type and its behaviors, and its states
and transitions to the type's Workflow config. A type takes one.

Says how a UI renders the field's control: `@display({ multiline: true })`
asks for one that holds several lines. It adds no storage or validation,
and changes no generated code. A field takes one; an operation and an
argument take none.

- On a type declaration or a field.

### `@docs`

```ts
function docs(config: { readonly title: string }): PropertyDecorator
```

Short human-facing label for the field: JSON Schema `title`.

- On a field.

### `@icon`

```ts
function icon(name: string): PropertyDecorator
```

Name of the glyph a UI shows for the field: `x-icon`. The core accepts any
name; a distribution may restrict it to an icon set.

- On a field.

### `@internalMetadata`

```ts
const internalMetadata: PropertyDecorator
```

Marks the field as dispatch metadata, such as a union member's discriminator, rather than user-facing data.

- On a field.

### `@purpose`

```ts
function purpose(markdown: string): PropertyDecorator
```

Longer-form Markdown explaining what the field is for: `x-purpose`.

- On a field.

### `@strictJSON`

```ts
const strictJSON: ClassDecorator
```

Make every generated decoder of the type (Go, TypeScript, Python, Rust)
reject a key the type does not declare and a required field that is absent
or null. Applies to this object only: a nested object type opts in on its
own.

- On a type declaration.

### `@temporalFormat`

```ts
function temporalFormat(format: TemporalWireFormat): PropertyDecorator
```

Declares the wire encoding of a Temporal.DateTime field whose source sends
a bare epoch count instead of ISO text. The unit is a fact
about the source API and is never guessed from the digit count. Serializes
as the `temporalFormat` IR field (`x-temporal-format` in the legacy
JSON-Schema wire form). Only valid on Temporal.DateTime fields.

- On a field.

### `@trait`

```ts
function trait(options: TraitOptions = {}): ClassDecorator
```

Marks a configurable trait. Introduce a trait only when fields need
per-implementer configuration, multiple traits must compose, and at least
two concrete schema types need the mechanism today.

- On a type declaration.

### `@uiControl`

```ts
function uiControl(control: UIControl): PropertyDecorator
```

The control a schema form draws for the field, in place of the one it picks (UIControl).

- On a field.

### Type wrappers and bases

```ts
type ValidateConfig = {
  readonly min?: number;
  readonly max?: number;
  /** Largest multipart upload in bytes; only on a file-upload scalar field. */
  readonly uploadMaxBytes?: number;
  readonly minLength?: number;
  readonly maxLength?: number;
  readonly listMin?: number;
  readonly listMax?: number;
  readonly pattern?: string;
  readonly format?: string;
}
```

The rules `Validate<T, C>` adds, which every generated decoder checks:
`min` and `max` bound a number, `minLength` and `maxLength` a text,
`listMin` and `listMax` a list's length, and `pattern` is a regular
expression a text must match.

```ts
type Wrapped<T> = { readonly __wrapped: T }
```

The phantom base of every wrapper below: it carries the wrapped type and
is never set. A wrapper is an intersection with T, from which a
conditional type cannot take T back; through the base it can
(`F extends Wrapped<infer T> ? T : F`), so a mapped type unwraps a field's
type, as `@superschematic/stack` types an environment's `env`.

```ts
type Default<T, V> = T & Wrapped<T> & { readonly __default: V }
```

The decoders fill in `V` when a payload leaves the field out.

```ts
type PlatformDefault<T> = T & Wrapped<T> & { readonly __platformDefault: true }
```

```ts
type Nullable<T> = T | null
```

The field may be absent or null; `name?: T` means the same.

```ts
type Validate<T, C extends ValidateConfig> = T & Wrapped<T> & { readonly __validate: C }
```

`T` with the rules of `C` (ValidateConfig), which every generated decoder checks.

```ts
type Secret<T> = T & Wrapped<T> & { readonly __secret: true }
```

A value kept out of logs: mask helpers clear it, and an `@envVars` loader marks it secret.

### Types the declarations name

```ts
type BehaviorName = keyof BehaviorConfigs
```

A name @behavior takes: a key of BehaviorConfigs.

```ts
type BehaviorConfigArg<N extends BehaviorName> =
  undefined extends BehaviorConfigs[N]
    ? [config?: BehaviorConfigs[N]]
    : Record<string, never> extends BehaviorConfigs[N]
      ? [config?: BehaviorConfigs[N]]
      : [config: BehaviorConfigs[N]]
```

The config argument of @behavior(name, config): optional when the
behavior takes no config or every key of its config is optional.

```ts
type UIControl =
  | 'slider'
  | 'number-field'
  | 'switch'
  | 'segmented'
  | 'radio'
  | 'select'
  | 'combobox'
  | 'checkboxes'
  | 'input'
  | 'textarea'
```

The control a schema form draws for a field, in place of the one it picks
from the field's type and `Validate` limits: `uiControl` in the IR.

- `slider`, `number-field`: a number. A slider needs a finite min and max.
- `switch`, `segmented`, `radio`, `select`, `combobox`: an enum. A switch
  needs two values that read as on and off.
- `checkboxes`, `combobox`: an array of an enum.
- `input`, `textarea`: a string.
A form ignores a control that does not fit the field and picks its own.

```ts
type TemporalWireFormat =
  | 'unix'
  | 'unix_millis'
  | 'unix_micros'
  | 'unix_nanos'
```

Wire encodings for @temporalFormat: the epoch units. ISO text is the
default and is never declared.

```ts
type DisplayTone = "muted" | "active" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"
```

What a state means to a reader, which a UI maps onto its own colors:
`muted` for a state nothing happens in (a draft, a backlog), `active`
for one work is under way in, `success` and `danger` for one that went
well or badly, `warning` for one that needs attention.

```ts
interface DisplayState {
  /** The state's label: "In review". */
  readonly label?: string;
  /** The present-progressive form a UI shows while an instance is in the state: "Implementing". */
  readonly activeForm?: string;
  readonly tone?: DisplayTone;
}
```

How a UI shows one Workflow state. Give at least one member.

```ts
interface DisplayConfig {
  /** What to call one instance: "Ticket". */
  readonly noun?: string;
  /** What to call several: "Tickets". */
  readonly plural?: string;
  /**
   * The field whose value is an instance's title: one of the type's own
   * fields, holding a single text value (a string, or a scalar whose
   * values are strings), neither secret nor uiHidden.
   */
  readonly titleField?: string;
  /** What a button that creates an instance says: "New ticket". */
  readonly createLabel?: string;
  /**
   * The glyph a UI shows beside the type's name: "receipt". It is a name
   * an app's icon set draws, a letter or a digit, then letters, digits,
   * `.`, `_`, `:`, `/` and `-` ("mdi:receipt", "solid/box"); which names
   * exist is the app's rule.
   */
  readonly icon?: string;
  /**
   * The fields that summarize an instance in a list, in order: the type's
   * own fields, by name, or fields its behaviors add, by qualified name,
   * the behavior's name, a dot and the field's: "Workflow.status".
   */
  readonly summaryFields?: readonly string[];
  /** Labels of states of the type's Workflow, by state. */
  readonly states?: Readonly<Record<string, DisplayState>>;
  /**
   * Labels of transitions of the type's Workflow, by the state a
   * transition leaves, then by the state it enters:
   * `{ todo: { doing: "Start" } }`.
   */
  readonly transitions?: Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, string>>>>;
}
```

@display's argument. Give at least one member.

```ts
interface FieldDisplayConfig {
  /**
   * A control of several lines (true) or one line (false), whatever the
   * field's maxLength. The field must hold text, or a list of text, and
   * must not be secret.
   */
  readonly multiline?: boolean;
}
```

@display's argument on a field. Give one member.

```ts
type TraitOptions = {
  readonly prefix?: string;
}
```

## `@superschematic/db`

### `@column`

```ts
function column(source: string | ProjectionFunctionCall): PropertyDecorator
```

Names the `alias.field` a projection column reads, or computes it with a
SQL function the migrations own. A function column has the field's
declared type and nullability; the function must honor them.

- On a field, only in DB schemas.

### `@conflictUnit`

```ts
function conflictUnit(strategy: ConflictUnitStrategy): PropertyDecorator
```

Sets the merge unit of a graph member's field.

- On a field.

### `@graphMember`

```ts
function graphMember(options: GraphMemberOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Marks an entity kind of a version graph. The member must be @versioned,
with one UUID @key, exactly one relation to the root and no deletedAt.
superschematic adds its entityKey, ref and deletedOnRef fields.

- On a type declaration.

### `@index`

```ts
function index<T>(
  keys: readonly (keyof T)[],
  uniqueOrOptions?: boolean | IndexOptions,
): ClassDecorator
```

An index over the listed fields, unique when asked; the engine keeps it too.

- On a type declaration.

### `@join`

```ts
function join<TTable>(
  alias: string,
  on: Readonly<Record<string, string>>,
  kind?: "inner" | "left",
): ClassDecorator
```

Adds a joined table to a @projection under `alias`. `on` maps
`alias.field` to `otherAlias.field` equalities (schema field names, not
SQL). `kind` defaults to "inner"; a "left" join makes every column read
through the alias nullable.

- On a type declaration, only in DB schemas.

### `@jsonField`

```ts
const jsonField: PropertyDecorator
```

Stores the field as JSONB.

- On a type declaration or a field.
- Also exported by `@superschematic/schema`.

### `@key`

```ts
const key: PropertyDecorator
```

The table's primary key; in the engine, a unique field.

- On a field.

### `@optimistic`

```ts
const optimistic: ClassDecorator
```

Gives a DB table the _version column, the trigger that bumps it on every
update and the fenced writes UpdateOneIfVersion and DeleteOneIfVersion,
with no history. @versioned implies it, so a type carries one or the other.

- On a type declaration.

### `@projection`

```ts
function projection<TSource>(options: ProjectionOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a projection view: a read-only relation over the source table
`TSource` (addressed as `base`) and any `@join` tables. The class fields
are the view's columns; each reads `base.<field>` unless `@column` says
otherwise. superschematic generates the Postgres view, its migration and
its Arrow schema from this one declaration. Only DB schemas declare
projections, and a projection is never a table or a language type.

- On a type declaration, only in DB schemas.

### `@queue`

```ts
function queue(options?: QueueOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a queue of the DB service whose class is its message
(docs/stack-model.md, section 8.8). The class's fields are the message's;
the database holds the queue in a table of its own, and an API's
`@worker` handles its messages:

```ts
@queue({ retries: 5, backoff: "30s" })
export abstract class OrderPlaced {
  orderId: Identity.UUID;
}
```

- On a type declaration, only in DB schemas.

### `@searchField`

```ts
const searchField: PropertyDecorator
```

Joins the field into the table's trigram-indexed `search_text` column.

- On a field.

### `@sourceMustProject`

```ts
const sourceMustProject: PropertyDecorator
```

Marks a field that @source projections are expected to carry. A projection
omitting the field draws a verification warning instead of the usual
silent removal.

- On a field.

### `@unique`

```ts
const unique: PropertyDecorator
```

A unique constraint on the column; in the engine, unique within a namespace, which lookup reads by.

- On a field.

### `@versionGraph`

```ts
function versionGraph<TFunction extends Function>(target: TFunction): void
function versionGraph(options?: VersionGraphOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Marks the root of a version graph: the stable identity its member rows
and generated graph tables reference. The root has one UUID @key and is
never overlaid. superschematic generates the graph's ref, commit and
patch tables and their enums from the declarations.

- On a type declaration.

### `@versioned`

```ts
function versioned<TFunction extends Function>(target: TFunction): void
function versioned(options?: VersionedOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Keeps every version of a row: a history table, and writes fenced by version.

- On a type declaration.

### Type wrappers and bases

```ts
type OnDeleteAction = "CASCADE" | "RESTRICT" | "NO ACTION"
```

FK ON DELETE actions expressible on a relation. SET NULL is intentionally
omitted: it needs a nullable FK column, and relations are non-null.

```ts
type RelationOptions = { onDelete?: OnDeleteAction }
```

Options carried by a relation's second type argument. onDelete controls the
generated FK's ON DELETE action; omitting it keeps the default (CASCADE).

```ts
type Relation<T, Opts extends RelationOptions = {}> = T & { readonly __relation: true }
```

Opts is a constrained phantom: the `extends RelationOptions` bound gives the
author typecheck and autocomplete on the option value, while the superschematic Go
loader reads the actual value from the second type-argument node (mirroring
Validate<T, C>). No embed is added because nothing reads a `__relationOpts`.

```ts
type HasMany<T> = T[] & { readonly __hasMany: true }
```

The rows of T whose relation points at this row.

```ts
type ManyToMany<T> = T[] & { readonly __manyToMany: true }
```

```ts
type AutoGenerate<T> = T & { readonly __autogen: true }
```

The database generates the value on insert.

```ts
type JsonField<T> = T & { readonly __jsonField: true }
```

The field is stored as JSONB.

### Types the declarations name

```ts
interface VersionedPruneReference {
  /** Referencing table name (snake_case, as in DDL). */
  readonly table: string;
  /** Referencing table's column holding the versioned row key. */
  readonly keyColumn: string;
  /** Referencing table's column holding the pinned _version. */
  readonly versionColumn: string;
}
```

```ts
interface VersionedOptions {
  readonly retentionDays?: number;
  readonly partitionBy?: "month";
  /**
   * Keep history rows whose (key, _version) pair is referenced by these tables
   * out of the generated prune function, so externally pinned row images
   * survive retention. Requires retentionDays.
   *
   * Takes one reference or a list of them: a versioned table can have several
   * independent readers of its historical rows, and each needs its own
   * exclusion. Declaring a second reference never displaces the first.
   *
   * Verification checks that this implies retentionDays, that every
   * identifier is snake_case (they are interpolated into DDL), and that no
   * reference is repeated. When the table is a DB type of the same schema, it
   * also checks that keyColumn has the versioned key's type and that
   * versionColumn is a Generic.Int64 column; a table outside the schema is
   * checked syntactically only. It cannot check the dangerous direction: a
   * table that declares retentionDays and has as-of readers but does NOT
   * declare the exclusion that protects them prunes their pinned images with
   * no diagnostic. Nothing in superschematic knows who reads a table's history, so that
   * one stays on the schema author and on repo-local tests.
   */
  readonly pruneKeepReferencedBy?: VersionedPruneReference | readonly VersionedPruneReference[];
  /**
   * Fields (schema field names) left out of every history image: the row an
   * insert or update records and a delete's tombstone. The history readers
   * return their zero value. The key, deletedAt and relations cannot be
   * excluded, and a @graphMember may exclude only fields whose conflict unit
   * is "excluded" and the audit fields.
   */
  readonly exclude?: readonly string[];
}
```

```ts
interface ProjectionSettingBinding {
  readonly column: string;
  readonly setting: string;
  readonly optional?: boolean;
}
```

One `column = setting` binding of a @projection row rule. `column` is an
`alias.field` reference to a schema field (camelCase): the alias is `base`
for the projection's source table or a `@join` alias. superschematic
resolves it to the SQL column and the cast; the declaration never carries
SQL.

Generated as `column = current_setting(setting)::<column type>`. An unset
setting makes `current_setting` raise, so the view fails closed.
`optional: true` reads `NULLIF(current_setting(setting, true), '')`
instead, so an unset or empty setting matches no row; use it inside
`anyOf`, where another binding can admit the row.

```ts
interface ProjectionFunctionCall {
  /** `schema.function`; never SQL text. */
  readonly function: string;
  /** `alias.field` references, passed in order. No literals or expressions. */
  readonly args: readonly string[];
}
```

A structured call to a SQL function the migrations own.

```ts
type ProjectionLiteral = string | number | boolean
```

A literal the column is compared to.

```ts
type ProjectionPredicate = (
  | ProjectionSettingBinding
  | { readonly anyOf: readonly ProjectionSettingBinding[] }
  | { readonly column: string; readonly isNull: true }
  | { readonly column: string; readonly notNull: true }
  | { readonly column: string; readonly equals: ProjectionLiteral }
  | (ProjectionFunctionCall & { readonly requiredSettings: readonly string[] })
) & {
  /**
   * Apply the rule only to rows where `when.column` equals `when.equals`;
   * every other row passes. Generated as
   * `(guard IS DISTINCT FROM 'literal' OR rule)`.
   */
  readonly when?: { readonly column: string; readonly equals: string };
}
```

One row rule of a @projection view, all ANDed:

- a binding `{ column, setting, optional? }`;
- `{ anyOf: [binding, binding, ...] }`, of which one must hold;
- a literal rule `{ column, isNull: true }`, `{ column, notNull: true }` or
  `{ column, equals: literal }`, which reads no setting;
- a function rule `{ function, args, requiredSettings }`: the function must
  return true, and every listed setting must be set.

```ts
type ProjectionOrder =
  | { readonly column: string; readonly rank: readonly string[] }
  | {
      readonly column: string;
      readonly direction?: "asc" | "desc";
      readonly nulls?: "first" | "last";
    }
```

One ORDER BY term of a `collapse`: either `rank`, the column's literal
values in winning order (every other value ranks last), or a `direction`
with an optional `nulls` placement.

```ts
interface ProjectionCollapse {
  /** The `alias.field` columns that identify one row (DISTINCT ON). */
  readonly by: readonly string[];
  /** Ranks the rows that share a key; the first wins. */
  readonly order?: readonly ProjectionOrder[];
}
```

```ts
interface ProjectionOptions {
  /** The Postgres schema the view is created in; readers address it as `pool.name`. */
  readonly pool: string;
  /** The view's name inside the pool. */
  readonly name: string;
  /**
   * The 14-digit version stamp of the generated migration. An applied
   * migration is never rewritten: a changed declaration takes a new stamp.
   */
  readonly migration: string;
  /** The row rules, all ANDed, in order. */
  readonly where?: readonly ProjectionPredicate[];
  /**
   * Keep one row per key: the view is generated with `DISTINCT ON (by)` and
   * `ORDER BY by, order`, so the first row in that order wins.
   */
  readonly collapse?: ProjectionCollapse;
}
```

```ts
interface IndexOptions {
  readonly unique?: boolean;
  readonly name?: string;
}
```

```ts
type SchemaClass = abstract new (...args: never[]) => unknown
```

A schema class, referenced as a value in a decorator argument.

```ts
type QueueOptions = {
  /** How many times a message whose handler fails is handled again before it is dead; five unless set. */
  readonly retries?: number;
  /**
   * How long a message that failed once waits before it is due again, a duration of whole seconds (`"30s"`, `"5m"`);
   * thirty seconds unless set. Each later failure doubles the wait, up to maxBackoff.
   */
  readonly backoff?: string;
  /** The longest wait a failure doubles to, a duration of whole seconds, the backoff or more; an hour unless set, or the backoff when that is longer. */
  readonly maxBackoff?: string;
  /** How long a claim holds a message unless its worker extends it, a duration of whole seconds; a minute unless set. */
  readonly lease?: string;
  /** How long a done message stays before a worker removes it, a duration of whole seconds (`"168h"`); `"0s"` removes it when it is done; a week unless set. Dead messages stay. */
  readonly retain?: string;
}
```

The options of a queue: how often a failed message is retried, and when, and how long a done one stays.

```ts
interface VersionGraphOptions {
  /**
   * Prefixes the generated graph tables (snake_case) and types (PascalCase).
   * Defaults to the root's name.
   */
  readonly name?: string;
  /** Recorded on every commit of the graph. Defaults to 0. */
  readonly schemaEpoch?: number;
  /**
   * A commit this many commits past the nearest snapshot on its chain is
   * snapshotted, so reading its tree stops there. Positive; defaults to 64.
   */
  readonly snapshotEvery?: number;
}
```

```ts
interface GraphParent {
  readonly key: string;
  readonly of: SchemaClass;
}
```

Containment: the field `key` holds the parent row's entityKey, and `of` is
a member type of the same graph, the member itself included.

```ts
interface GraphMemberOptions {
  /** The graph's root: the @versionGraph type. */
  readonly graph: SchemaClass;
  readonly parent?: GraphParent;
  /** An Int64 field that orders siblings. */
  readonly order?: string;
  /** At most one live row of the kind per ref. */
  readonly singleton?: boolean;
}
```

```ts
type ConflictUnitStrategy = "atomic" | "keyed" | "jsonSchema" | "excluded"
```

The merge unit of a graph member's field. `atomic` (the default) is the
whole field; `keyed` is each top-level key of a JSON object; `jsonSchema`
treats a JSON Schema object as units; `excluded` is not content.

## `@superschematic/api`

### `@allowService`

```ts
function allowService(cfg?: ServiceCallersConfig): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator
```

Beside the operation's user clause, which it needs: an end user who meets
the clause, or a listed service with no end user, which then stands in
for the user. On a class, every operation without its own clause that is
not @publicRoute.

- On an operation set or an operation.

### `@auth`

```ts
const auth: MethodDecorator
```

The route needs a caller.

- On an operation.

### `@bodyLimit`

```ts
function bodyLimit(cfg: BodyLimitConfig): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator
```

Bounds the size of a route's request body; on a class, each route of the set's.

- On an operation set or an operation.

### `@deriver`

```ts
function deriver(options?: DeriverOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a deriver of the API service: a deployable that fills the
Derived fields of the engine types of the API's database (D74). It pulls
the stale fields, calls the project's generated Derivers for each, which
asks a model, and settles the answers. The class's name is the
deriver's, and the class holds nothing:

```ts
@deriver({ schemas: ["Ticket"], concurrency: 4 })
export abstract class TriageTickets {}
```

- On a type declaration, only in API schemas.

### `@docs`

```ts
function docs(config: DocsConfig): MethodDecorator
```

The operation's documentation.

- On an operation.

### `@encrypted`

```ts
const encrypted: MethodDecorator
```

The route's request body travels as an encrypted envelope.

- On an operation.

### `@hmacVerified`

```ts
function hmacVerified(cfg: HmacVerifiedConfig): MethodDecorator
```

Every server checks the request's signature with the provider's verifier
first, before the rate limit, the body limit and the permission check.

- On an operation.

### `@icon`

```ts
function icon(name: string): MethodDecorator
```

The glyph of the operation's MCP tool. Any name unless an extension restricts it.

- On an operation.

### `@job`

```ts
function job(options?: JobOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a job of the API service: a run to completion that does the
API's background work with the API's Deps (docs/stack-model.md, section
8.7). The class's name is the job's, and the class holds nothing:

```ts
@job({ schedule: "*\/15 * * * *", timeout: "10m" })
export abstract class ExpireCarts {}
```

- On a type declaration, only in API schemas.

### `@manualRouteRegistration`

```ts
const manualRouteRegistration: MethodDecorator
```

Each router gates the route and hands it to a handler the implementation
writes: TypeScript's from `manualRoutes`, Go's from `Config.ManualRoutes`,
Rust's from `build_router_with_manual_routes`.

- On an operation.

### `@mcp`

```ts
function mcp(config: MCPConfig): MethodDecorator
```

Publishes the operation as an MCP tool, or says why it is not one.

- On an operation.

### `@paginated`

```ts
function paginated(cfg?: PaginatedConfig): MethodDecorator
```

The operation's list result pages by an opaque cursor (D60): a GET whose
result is a list takes the query parameters `cursor` and `limit` and
answers `{ items, next }`, `next` null after the last page.

- On an operation, only in API schemas.

### `@publicRoute`

```ts
const publicRoute: MethodDecorator
```

Anyone may call the route, in an `Authenticated` set too. Refused with
`@auth`, `@requirePermission` or `@requireOwnership`.

- On an operation.

### `@rateLimit`

```ts
function rateLimit(cfg: RateLimitConfig): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator
```

Bounds a route's requests per minute; on a class, each route of the set's.

- On an operation set or an operation.

### `@requireOwnership`

```ts
const requireOwnership: MethodDecorator
```

The route needs a caller; the implementation checks that the caller owns what it touches.

- On an operation.

### `@requirePermission`

```ts
function requirePermission(perms: readonly string[]): MethodDecorator
```

The route needs a caller holding one of the permissions.

- On an operation.

### `@requireService`

```ts
function requireService(cfg?: ServiceCallersConfig): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator
```

Only a listed service may call. With a user clause (@auth, an
Authenticated set, @requirePermission, @requireOwnership), it must forward
an end user who meets it; without one, no end user is looked at. On a
class, every operation without its own clause that is not @publicRoute.

- On an operation set or an operation.

### `@rest`

```ts
function rest(method: HttpMethod, path?: string): MethodDecorator
```

The route's HTTP method and path, under `/api`.

- On an operation.

### `@source`

```ts
function source(target: unknown): ClassDecorator
```

The class is a view of a table: its fields are checked against the table's.

- On a type declaration, only in API or General schemas.
- Also exported by `@superschematic/schema`.

### `@timeout`

```ts
function timeout(cfg: TimeoutConfig): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator
```

Bounds how long a route's request may take; on a class, each route of the set's.

- On an operation set or an operation.

### `@uiHidden`

```ts
const uiHidden: PropertyDecorator
```

A UI schema renderer hides the field.

- On a field.
- Also exported by `@superschematic/schema`.

### `@userAdministration`

```ts
function userAdministration(cfg?: UserAdministrationConfig): ClassDecorator
```

The user model's administration routes, on a class with no methods:
superschematic adds the routes that create, list, disable and enable
users and set a password; list, create, update and delete roles; and
grant and revoke them. Each needs a permission under the naming key
identity_permission_prefix: identity.users.read or .users.write,
identity.roles.read or .roles.write. The identity runtime serves them,
so the implementation has no method for them. The API's authDb must name
a DB schema with a User and a UserRole table, and an API takes one such
class, which takes no Authenticated or Encrypted base and no service
clause.

- On an operation set.

### `@userSessions`

```ts
function userSessions(cfg?: UserSessionsConfig): ClassDecorator
```

The user model's session routes, on a class with no methods:
superschematic adds login, logout, me, capabilities and changePassword
under the path, and register with `register: true`. The identity runtime
serves them, so the implementation has no method for them. The API's
authDb must name a DB schema with a User table, and an API takes one
such class. The class takes no Authenticated or Encrypted base and no
service clause: each route's rule is the model's.

- On an operation set.

### `@virtual`

```ts
const virtual: PropertyDecorator
```

A field of a `@source` view with no column behind it, which the implementation fills in.

- On a field.
- Also exported by `@superschematic/schema`.

### `@webhook`

```ts
const webhook: MethodDecorator
```

An operation a third party calls: no SDK has a method or a tool for it.

- On an operation.

### `@worker`

```ts
function worker(options: WorkerOptions): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a worker of the API service: a deployable that claims the
messages of a queue of the API's database and handles each with the API's
Deps (docs/stack-model.md, section 8.8). The class's name is the
worker's, and the class holds nothing:

```ts
@worker({ queue: OrderPlaced, concurrency: 4 })
export abstract class FulfilOrders {}
```

- On a type declaration, only in API schemas.

### Type wrappers and bases

```ts
type QueryParam<T> = T & { readonly __queryParam: true }
```

Read the argument from the query string.

```ts
type EncryptedField<T> = T & { readonly __encrypted: true }
```

The operation's request body travels as an encrypted envelope.

```ts
type RefersToConfig<Target> = {
  /** The operation that lists the targets: "listProducts" or "ProductCatalog.listProducts". The API's one operation that lists them when unsaid. */
  readonly options?: string;
  /** The target's field the value holds: "id" unsaid. */
  readonly value?: keyof Target & string;
  /** The target's field that names an item: its @display titleField unsaid. */
  readonly label?: keyof Target & string;
}
```

Which operation lists a reference's targets, and which of their fields it holds and shows (D61).

```ts
type RefersTo<T, Target, C extends RefersToConfig<Target> = {}> = T & {
  readonly __refersTo: { readonly target: Target; readonly config: C };
}
```

A value that names an item of Target, as an operation of this API lists
it (D61): `RefersTo<Identity.UUID, ProductView>`, or with its config,
`RefersTo<Identity.UUID, ProductView, { options: "listProducts" }>`. A
list refers element by element: `RefersTo<Identity.UUID, ProductView>[]`.

```ts
type SearchQuery<T extends string = string> = (T & { readonly __queryParam: true; readonly __search: true }) | null
```

The operation's search text: an optional query parameter whose words each
item's searchable text contains (D62). An operation takes one.

```ts
type SortBy<Item, Fields extends readonly (keyof Item & string)[]> =
  | ((Fields[number] | `-${Fields[number]}`) & { readonly __queryParam: true; readonly __sortBy: Fields })
  | null
```

The order a paged list is read in (D60, amended): a field Fields names,
ascending, or after a "-", descending; ties break by the item's id in
the same direction. @paginated's defaultSort is the order when none is
sent. An operation takes one.

```ts
abstract class Authenticated {}
```

Every route of an operation set that extends it needs a caller.

```ts
abstract class Encrypted {}
```

Every route of an operation set that extends it takes its request body as an encrypted envelope.

### Types the declarations name

```ts
type RateLimitConfig = {
  readonly requestsPerMinute: number;
}
```

```ts
type BodyLimitConfig = {
  readonly megabytes: number;
}
```

```ts
type TimeoutConfig = {
  readonly seconds: number;
}
```

```ts
type HmacVerifiedConfig = {
  readonly provider: string;
}
```

```ts
type ServiceHandleRef = {
  readonly __brand: "ServiceHandle";
  readonly name: string;
  readonly kind: "API";
}
```

An API service's handle: the sentinel an API service exports from its
src/service.generated.ts, built by service() in
@superschematic/schema-config. Every ServiceHandle<"API"> is one, and a
handle of another kind is not. The shape is restated here because the
authoring packages do not depend on one another.

```ts
type ServiceCallersConfig = {
  /**
   * API service handles: the servers that serve those APIs may call. Each
   * must be an API service. Without from, every server with a calls edge
   * to this API in the stack may; from narrows the edges, never widens
   * them.
   */
  readonly from?: readonly ServiceHandleRef[];
}
```

The services an operation's service clause admits.

```ts
type DocsLifecycle = "draft" | "experimental" | "active" | "deprecated" | "retired"
```

```ts
type DocsVisibility = "public" | "internal" | "preview"
```

```ts
type DocsMappingStatus = "mapped" | "uncertain"
```

```ts
type DocsReplayMode = "read_only" | "idempotent" | "compare_and_swap"
```

The replay guarantee an operation gives a caller that repeats a call.

```ts
type DocsConfig = {
  /** Short name: the OpenAPI summary. */
  readonly title: string;
  /** The OpenAPI description; it replaces the operation's comment there. */
  readonly description: string;
  /** Stable dotted identifier, at least two lowercase segments: "orders.returns.create". */
  readonly capability: string;
  /** deprecated and retired mark the OpenAPI operation deprecated. */
  readonly lifecycle: DocsLifecycle;
  /** How the operation appears in documentation; it grants no access. */
  readonly visibility: DocsVisibility;
  /** The primary reader. Open to any value unless an extension restricts it. */
  readonly audience?: string;
  /** Defaults to "mapped". */
  readonly mappingStatus?: DocsMappingStatus;
  /** What replaces a deprecated or retired operation. */
  readonly replacement?: string;
  /** The date the operation stops being served, YYYY-MM-DD. */
  readonly sunset?: string;
  /** The replay guarantee; generators never infer one. */
  readonly replayMode?: DocsReplayMode;
  /** RFC 6901 pointers into the generated tool arguments to the idempotency keys. */
  readonly idempotencyKeyPointers?: readonly string[];
  /** RFC 6901 pointers into the generated tool arguments to the expected revision. */
  readonly expectedRevisionPointers?: readonly string[];
  /** When a caller, a person or a model, should choose this operation. */
  readonly useWhen?: string;
  /** When a caller should choose another operation instead. */
  readonly doNotUseWhen?: string;
  /** The outcome a caller should expect after a successful call. */
  readonly success?: string;
  /** The operation's expected errors and the usual correction for each. */
  readonly errors?: readonly DocsError[];
}
```

The reader-facing documentation of one operation.

```ts
type DocsError = {
  readonly code: string;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly commonCorrection: string;
}
```

One expected error of an operation. Codes are unique, ignoring case.

```ts
type MCPInvocationPolicy = "auto" | "ask"
```

The core's invocation policy values: "auto" (the default) lets an MCP
client run the tool when a model calls it; "ask" has the client ask the
person first.

```ts
interface MCPToolOptions {
  /** Whether an MCP client runs the tool when a model calls it ("auto", the default) or asks the person first ("ask"). */
  readonly invocationPolicy?: MCPInvocationPolicy;
}
```

The options a visible tool's @mcp takes besides its handle and _meta. The
core declares its invocation policy key here.

An extension that registers its own invocation policy
(Registry.RegisterToolInvocationPolicy) adds its key from its authoring
package by module augmentation:

    declare module "@superschematic/api" {
      interface MCPToolOptions {
        readonly review?: "never" | "always";
      }
    }

The registry decides which key a build accepts. With an extension's policy
registered the core key still type-checks and fails the load.

```ts
type MCPConfig =
  | (MCPToolOptions & {
      /** The tool's wire identifier: lowercase snake_case, at most 48 characters, unique in the API. */
      readonly handle: string;
      readonly hidden?: false;
      /** Copied into the tool's MCP _meta object as written. */
      readonly _meta?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
    })
  | {
      readonly hidden: true;
      /** Why the operation is not a tool. */
      readonly reason: string;
    }
```

An operation's MCP classification. A visible tool takes its title and
description from @docs and its icon from @icon; a hidden operation says
why it is not a tool.

```ts
type PaginatedConfig = {
  /** How many items a page holds when the caller sends no limit: 20, or maxLimit when that is less. */
  readonly defaultLimit?: number;
  /** The most items a caller may ask a page to hold: 1 to 1000, 100 when left out. */
  readonly maxLimit?: number;
  /** The order of a request that sends no sort: one of the SortBy argument's values (D60, amended). */
  readonly defaultSort?: string;
}
```

```ts
type UserSessionsConfig =
  | {
      readonly path?: string;
      readonly login?: true;
      readonly register?: boolean;
    }
  | {
      readonly path?: string;
      readonly login: false;
      readonly register?: false;
    }
```

The routes @userSessions adds. `path` prefixes them, "auth" by default.
`login`, true by default, adds login, logout and changePassword; false
leaves me and capabilities, for an API whose users sign in through
another API of the same authDb. `register`, false by default, adds
register, which anyone may call, and needs the login.

```ts
type UserAdministrationConfig = {
  readonly path?: string;
}
```

The routes @userAdministration adds. `path` prefixes them, "auth/admin" by default.

```ts
type JobOptions = {
  /**
   * A five-field cron: minute, hour, day of the month, month and day of the
   * week (`"*\/15 * * * *"`). Without one the job runs only on demand. An
   * environment's settings change it or turn it off.
   */
  readonly schedule?: string;
  /** The IANA time zone the schedule is read in (`"Europe/Paris"`); UTC unless set. */
  readonly timeZone?: string;
  /** Bounds one run, a duration of whole seconds (`"90s"`, `"10m"`, `"1h30m"`); ten minutes unless set. */
  readonly timeout?: string;
  /** How many times a failed run is run again; none unless set. */
  readonly retries?: number;
}
```

The options of a job: when it runs, and how long and how often it tries.

```ts
type WorkerOptions = {
  /** The `@queue` class whose messages the worker handles, imported from the API's database. */
  readonly queue: abstract new (...args: never[]) => unknown;
  /** How many messages an instance handles at a time; one unless set. An environment's settings change it. */
  readonly concurrency?: number;
  /** How long a stopping worker lets its running handlers finish before it gives their messages back, a duration of whole seconds; eight seconds unless set. */
  readonly grace?: string;
}
```

The options of a worker: the queue it handles, and how.

```ts
type DeriverOptions = {
  /** The names of the engine types of the API's database whose Derived fields the deriver fills; every type of it that composes Derived unless set. An API imports no engine type, so it names them. */
  readonly schemas?: readonly string[];
  /** How many answers an instance runs at a time; four unless set. An environment's settings change it. */
  readonly concurrency?: number;
  /** How many stale fields a pull asks for, 1 to 100; fifty unless set. */
  readonly batchSize?: number;
}
```

The options of a deriver: the engine types whose Derived fields it fills, and how.

```ts
enum HttpMethod {
  GET = "GET",
  POST = "POST",
  PUT = "PUT",
  PATCH = "PATCH",
  DELETE = "DELETE"
}
```

## `@superschematic/schema-config`

### `@envVars`

```ts
const envVars: ClassDecorator
```

On a class of a General or API schema: its fields are the service's
environment variables, with a generated loader and values-schema.json. On
an API it is the config of the API's server, whose fields a stack's `env`
binds.

- On a type declaration.

## `@superschematic/stack`

### `@database`

```ts
function database(options: { readonly hosts: readonly ServiceHandle<"DB">[] }): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a database that hosts several DB schemas.

- On a type declaration, only in Stack schemas.

### `@environment`

```ts
function environment<
  const T extends TargetName | undefined = undefined,
  const S extends readonly unknown[] = readonly [],
>(options: EnvironmentOptions<T, S>): ClassDecorator
```

Declares an environment: a target and the values only a person decides.
The target's values sit under its name (`gcp: { project, region }`), and
each settings element is typed by its `of`. A class that extends another
`@environment` class inherits its values.

- On a type declaration, only in Stack schemas.

### `@server`

```ts
function server(options: { readonly serves: readonly ServiceHandle<"API">[] }): ClassDecorator
```

Declares a server that serves several APIs in one process.

- On a type declaration, only in Stack schemas.

### `@stack`

```ts
function stack(options: {
  readonly deploy?: readonly ServiceHandle<"API" | "DB" | "Site">[];
  readonly expose?: readonly (ServiceHandle<"API" | "Site"> | DeployableClass)[];
}): ClassDecorator
```

Declares the stack: its entry points and what is reachable from outside.
A site (a Site service's handle) is always exposed, named in `expose` or
not, and each API it calls must be exposed (D55).

- On a type declaration, only in Stack schemas.

### Types the declarations name

```ts
interface Targets {
  /** The core's target: every server a process, every database on one Postgres container. */
  local: LocalTarget;
}
```

The targets an environment may name: the core's `local`, and each target
whose authoring package augments it with the target's environment values
and a settings type per deployable kind, which `@environment` checks
against.

```ts
declare module "@superschematic/stack" {
  interface Targets {
    gcp: { values: GcpValues; server: CloudRunSettings; database: CloudSqlSettings };
  }
}
```

```ts
interface LocalTarget {
  values: { postgresImage?: string; postgresPort?: number; storageImage?: string; storagePort?: number };
  server: { port?: number };
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  database: {};
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  job: {};
  site: { port?: number };
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  bucket: {};
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  worker: {};
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  runner: {};
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  deriver: {};
}
```

The core's `local` target, which `superschematic stack dev` runs
(docs/stack-model.md, section 8.3). Its values set the image and the host
port of the environment's Postgres container and of its storage emulator
(D54), a server's and a site's settings its port, and a database, a job,
a worker, a bucket, an engine's runner (D58) and a deriver (D74) take no
settings. A port
left out is derived from the stack, the environment and the deployable.

```ts
type TargetName = Extract<keyof Targets, string>
```

A target's name: a key of `Targets`.

```ts
type DeployableClass = abstract new (...args: never[]) => unknown
```

A declared deployable, an `@server` or `@database` class, named as a value
(`of: Backend`).

```ts
type ValuesOf<T> = [T] extends [TargetName]
  ? Targets[T] extends { readonly values: infer V }
    ? V
    : {}
  : never
```

The values a target takes, under its name in `@environment`.

```ts
type SettingsElement<T, E> = E extends { readonly of: infer Of }
  ? Exact<
      E extends { readonly job: unknown }
        ? JobElementOf<E extends { readonly platform: string } ? undefined : T, Of>
        : E extends { readonly worker: unknown }
          ? WorkerElementOf<E extends { readonly platform: string } ? undefined : T, Of>
          : E extends { readonly deriver: unknown }
            ? DeriverElementOf<E extends { readonly platform: string } ? undefined : T, Of>
            : E extends { readonly runner: unknown }
              ? RunnerElementOf<E extends { readonly platform: string } ? undefined : T, Of>
              : ElementOf<E extends { readonly platform: string } ? undefined : T, Of>,
      E
    > &
      (E extends { readonly env: infer V } ? { readonly env: Exact<EnvFor<Of>, V> } : {})
  : { readonly of: ServiceHandle<"API" | "DB" | "Site" | "Bucket"> | DeployableClass }
```

One settings element checked: its `of` picks the settings type, a `job`,
a `worker` or a `deriver` beside an API's handle makes it the element of
that job, worker or deriver, and `runner: true` beside a DB's handle that of the engine's
runner of the database; its env is the config's fields, and a key none
takes is refused. An element that names a platform, which may be another
target's, takes any settings key; the loader checks it against that
platform.

```ts
type EnvironmentOptions<T extends TargetName | undefined, S extends readonly unknown[]> = {
  /** The target that places every deployable no setting places elsewhere. */
  readonly target?: T;
  /** Where exposed servers are reached. */
  readonly domain?: string;
  /** The DNS platform that holds the domain's records, with its values: `{ cloudflare: { zone, zoneId } }`. */
  readonly dns?: { readonly [platform: string]: { readonly [value: string]: unknown } };
  /** Settings per deployable; `of` is a service handle, a Bucket's among them (D54), or a declared deployable's class, with `job`, `worker`, `deriver` or `runner: true` beside a handle for a job, a worker, a deriver or an engine's runner. */
  readonly settings?: S & { readonly [I in keyof S]: SettingsElement<T, S[I]> };
  /** Makes the environment a family, one member per value. */
  readonly parameters?: readonly string[];
} & { readonly [K in NoInfer<T> & string]?: ValuesOf<K> }
```

The argument of `@environment`.
